I was disgnosed in my teens. First - I'm sorry you have to deal with this. However, get yourself to an endocrinologist ASAP. All an OBGYN or GP can or will do is prescribe birth control pills, which only mask some of the symptoms. PCOS is imbalance of hormones, where the ovaries produce an excess of testosterone. That extra testosterone then fucks up the estrogen/progesterone balance, and voila- cysts everywhere. Adding more female hormones (progesterone analogs and synthetic estrogen) doesnt combat the extra testosterone floating around. The endocrinologist will confirm via blood work that you have PCOS (and not something else, because there are other potential causes) and then likely prescribe one of two different testosterone blocking medications - propecia or spironolactone. I'd suggest propecia if you have the choice, since spironolactone is a potassium sparing diuretic. It can take up to a few months to see improvement, but... might be worth a try if you haven't already been down this road.
